doc.title: Charles Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 23, 1997

title: Opening and working travel, New York competition
summary: Welcome, travel for work, playing in a play, and competition among saxophonists in Local 802.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: We are filming today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. It’s a pleasure for me to welcome as my guest Charles Davis, saxophonist.
Oh, thank you. Pleasure being here.
This isn’t your first trip through Upstate New York.
Do you have to travel outside New York a lot to keep working?
Well travel is part of working. Sometimes it’s to Utica. Recently I was up in Williamstown, Massachusetts, during six weeks of the summer, performing in a play.
You were performing in a play?
Well I was playing the saxophone, performing/playing the saxophone in the play. I didn’t have any actual lines.

That sounds interesting. As I was, for some reason today I was looking at the 802 Local book from, I think ‘95, and I got curious, and I added up all the saxophone players in Local 802, and it was over thirteen hundred players.
Oh, yeah, well that’s only the ones that’s in the Union.
I didn’t even think about that. So can I guess that there is extreme competition for work right in New York?
Well you could say that. Yes you can say it. Well if it’s something that’s an ongoing factor I guess in music, it’s always competition.
